name: Toledo
title: Holidays in Toledo
intro: A hilltop city wrapped in a river gorge, where churches, mosques and synagogues crowd together, just half an hour from Madrid. Here's what Toledo is like, when to go and how long to stay.
image_alt: The Alcázar of Toledo above the Alcántara bridge and old city walls
facts_note: The EU is bringing in new entry checks, so check the rules on GOV.UK before you book.
when_to_go: April, May, September and October are best for walking the steep streets. July and August are very hot. Winter is cold but sunny and quiet once the day-trippers leave. Corpus Christi in early summer brings a big procession.

things.name: Toledo Cathedral
things.blurb: One of Spain's greatest Gothic cathedrals, with paintings by El Greco and Goya.

things.name: Mirador del Valle
things.blurb: The classic view of the whole city across the river gorge.

things.name: Alcázar
things.blurb: The fortress on the hilltop, now an army museum.

things.name: Synagogue of Santa María la Blanca
things.blurb: White horseshoe arches in a medieval synagogue.

things.name: El Greco's Burial of the Count of Orgaz
things.blurb: His masterpiece, in the church of Santo Tomé.

things.name: Marzipan
things.blurb: Toledo's speciality, sold in shops all over the old town.

faqs.question: Is Toledo worth visiting?
faqs.answer: Yes. It's one of Spain's most historic cities, with Christian, Jewish and Moorish buildings packed onto one hill.

faqs.question: How many days do you need in Toledo?
faqs.answer: One day covers the highlights, but staying a night lets you see it quiet in the evening.

faqs.question: Can you do Toledo as a day trip from Madrid?
faqs.answer: Yes. The fast train takes about 33 minutes from Madrid Atocha.

faqs.question: What is the best time to visit Toledo?
faqs.answer: Spring and autumn, around 20 to 29°C. Summer is very hot.

faqs.question: How do you get to Toledo?
faqs.answer: Fly into Madrid, which has many flights from the UK, then take the fast train or a bus.
